q: 1. A diagonal scale is used to read ... dimensions
explain: A diagonal scale uses diagonal lines to subdivide the smallest division further, allowing three successive dimensions (units, tenths, hundredths) to be read directly.

q: 2. In a direct vernier, the smallest division of a vernier is ... the smallest division of its primary scale
explain: In a direct vernier, the vernier scale graduations are slightly shorter than the main scale graduations, and they increase in the same direction, allowing finer readings.

q: 3. Measurements taken with a wrong scale can be corrected by using the relation
options: true length = (correct scale/wrong scale) x measured length
true length = (correct scale/wrong scale)^2 x measured length
true length = (correct scale/wrong scale)^3 x measured length
explain: For linear measurements taken with a wrong scale, the correct relation is true length = (wrong scale/correct scale) x measured length; the given options invert this ratio, so none of these matches the correct formula.

q: 4. If x is the smallest division on the main scale and n are the number of divisions on the vernier, then the least count of the vernier is
explain: The least count of a vernier equals the smallest main scale division divided by the total number of divisions on the vernier scale, i.e., x/n.

q: 5. A tape of length l and weight 'w' kg/m is suspended at its ends with a pull of P kg, the sag correction is,
explain: The standard sag correction formula for a tape hanging in a catenary between supports is Cs = L*W2/(24P2) per span, where W = w*L is the total weight of the span.

q: 6. A well conditioned triangle has no angle less than
explain: A well-conditioned triangle keeps all its angles between 30 deg and 120 deg so that a small error in angle measurement causes only a small error in the plotted position of the point.

q: 7. A clinometer is used for
explain: A clinometer is a simple instrument used to measure the angle of slope (inclination) of the ground.

q: 8. Chain surveying is most suitable when
options: area to be surveyed is small
ground is fairly level and open with simple details
plans are required on a large scale
explain: Chain surveying works best under a combination of favourable conditions - small area, level open ground with simple details, and large-scale plan requirements - so all of these apply together.

q: 9. Then the position of a point is to be located accurately by a perpendicular offset, the direction of perpendicular is set out by means of
explain: To accurately set out a perpendicular offset direction from a chain line, an optical square (based on double reflection) is the standard instrument used.

q: 10. The accuracy in laying down the perpendicular offsets and in measuring them depends upon
explain: The accuracy of perpendicular offsets is influenced by several factors together - the plotting scale, offset length, and importance of the feature being located - so all of these apply.

q: 11. An instrument that can be used as an optical square is
explain: A box sextant, when set to read exactly 90 degrees, can be used in place of an optical square to set out right angles.

q: 12. The construction of optical square is based, on the principle of optical
explain: The optical square works on the principle of double reflection from two mirrors set at 45 degrees to each other, deflecting the line of sight through 90 degrees.

q: 13. Pick up the most accurate statement from the following
options: survey lines in an area should be as many as possible
number of base lines in an area is limited to one
main chain lines should from well conditioned triangles
oblique offsets are inferior to perpendicular offsets
explain: For accurate chain surveying, the framework of main chain lines should form well-conditioned triangles (angles not less than 30 nor more than 120 degrees), minimizing plotting errors.

q: 14. Reciprocal ranging is adopted when the following is encountered
explain: Reciprocal ranging is used when the end stations of a chain line are mutually invisible due to intervening obstacles like a river, where surveyors cannot see each other's ranging rods directly.

q: 15. A chain is made up mild steel or galvanized iron wire of diameter
explain: A standard surveying chain is made of mild steel or galvanized iron wire of about 4 mm diameter.

q: 16. Offsets are
explain: An offset is defined as a short lateral measurement taken from the chain line to locate a detail point lying off the chain line.

q: 17. When a chain is used at a temperature more than the temperature it was calibrated, the error in measured length will be
explain: A chain used at a higher temperature than its standardisation temperature expands, so it becomes effectively too long for every measurement, making the resulting error cumulative (in one consistent direction).

q: 18. It is more convenient and gives better results while measuring horizontal distance ... by stepping method
explain: Stepping method for measuring horizontal distance on sloping ground gives better, more convenient results when done downhill, since gravity assists in maintaining a horizontal tape segment.

q: 19. The permissible limits of error in chaining for measurement on rough of hilly ground is
explain: For chaining on rough or hilly ground, where conditions are difficult, a comparatively lower precision of about 1 in 250 is considered permissible.

q: 20. Offsets are
options: ties or check lines which are perpendicular to chain line
sets of minor instruments in chain surveying
chain lines which go out of alignment
explain: Offsets are lateral (typically short) measurements or ties, often perpendicular, taken from the chain line to locate the position of nearby details/objects.

q: 21. The tension, at which the effects of pull and sag for a tape are neutralised, is known as
explain: Normal tension is the specific value of pull at which the tape's elongation due to increased pull exactly balances the shortening effect due to reduced sag, neutralizing both effects.

q: 22. The length of a ranging rod should be
explain: A standard ranging rod is generally made 2 to 3 m long, painted in alternate red and white (or black) bands of 20 cm each for visibility.

q: 23. The principle of optics used in the construction of an optical square is
explain: An optical square works on the principle of double reflection, using two mirrors inclined at 45 deg to each other to deviate a ray of light through exactly 90 deg.

q: 24. Distance between two neighboring brass rings is
explain: In a standard surveying chain, brass rings (tally markers) are typically placed at every 20 cm interval (metre marks) to allow easy identification of sub-divisions.

q: 25. The main object of running a tie line is
options: to check accuracy of the work
to take details of nearby objects
to take offsets for detailed surveying
explain: The primary purpose of a tie line is to take offsets for detailed surveying of interior details that are located far from the main chain lines.

q: 26. The error in measured length due to incorrect holding of chain is
explain: Incorrect holding of the chain (not exactly along the line) sometimes lengthens and sometimes shortens the measured length randomly, so it is classified as a compensating (accidental) error.

q: 27. Long offsets are taken if the offset length exceeds
explain: When an offset exceeds 10 m in length, it is classified as a long offset and requires more careful (instrumental) methods to maintain perpendicularity/accuracy.

q: 28. One mile equals to
explain: Since a Gunter's chain is 66 feet long and one mile is 5280 feet, one mile equals 5280/66 = 80 Gunter's chains.

q: 29. Cross staff is an instrument used for
explain: A cross-staff's primary and specific function is to set out right angles (perpendicular offsets) from a chain line.

q: 30. Which of the following methods of offsets involves less measurements on the ground?
options: All involve equal measurements on the ground
explain: The method of perpendicular offsets requires fewer field measurements (just the offset length and its chainage) compared to oblique offsets or the method of ties, which need additional measurements to fully fix a point.

q: 31. The permissible error in chaining for measurement with chain on rough or hilly ground is
explain: On rough or hilly ground where chaining is more difficult, a relatively larger permissible error of 1 in 250 is allowed compared to smoother, level terrain.

q: 32. Survey is conducted at 40 C and the measured length was 5 km. If the chain was standardized at 20 C and co-efficient of linear expansion of chain material is 0.3 x 10^-5/C, then the correct length is
explain: Correction for temperature = L x coefficient x (T-T0) = 5000 x 0.3x10^-5 x 20 = 0.30 m; since survey temperature was higher than standardization temperature, the chain was elongated, so the correction is added: 5000 + 0.30 = 5000.30 m.

q: 33. For indirect ranging, number of ranging rods required is
explain: Indirect (random line/reciprocal) ranging typically requires a total of 5 ranging rods - two at the end stations and additional ones to establish and adjust the auxiliary intermediate points.

q: 34. For accurate work, the steel band should always be used in preference to chain because the steel band
options: is practically inextensible and is not liable to kinks when in use
can be easily repaired in the field
explain: A steel band is preferred for accurate work because it is practically inextensible (does not stretch like a chain's links/rings) and is not prone to kinking, giving more consistent, accurate measurements.

q: 35. Perpendicularity of an offset may be judged by eye, if the length of the offset is
explain: Perpendicularity of an offset can be judged sufficiently accurately by eye only for short offsets, up to about 5 m in length.

q: 36. The cross staff is carried out for
explain: As per the book's answer key, the cross staff is used in topographical survey work for setting out perpendicular offsets.

q: 37. Ranging in chain survey means
options: establishing an intermediate point on the line
determining the distance between end points
explain: Ranging in chain surveying specifically means the process of establishing intermediate points in a straight line between the end stations of a chain line.
